children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you through this assessment, I need to understand your situation better. Let me start with the first important question:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- Their age(s)
- If you have multiple children, their ages and names

The eligibility depends on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualifies automatically
- **16-19**: Need to check if they're in education or training
- **20 or older**: Generally not eligible

What are the details of the child/children you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have a son named **Alex who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age range, I need to check some additional details about his education or training status. Let me navigate to the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's current situation regarding education or training:

**Is Alex currently in education or training?**

This could include:
- School or college
- University or higher education
- An apprenticeship
- Other approved training courses

Or has he recently left education (within the last 20 weeks)?

Please let me know which applies to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is currently in education at sixth form college studying A-levels. Let me check the next step regarding the type and level of education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to verify that Alex's A-level education meets the specific eligibility requirements.

**A-levels are approved education, which is great!** However, I need to check a couple of additional details:

1. **Is Alex studying full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study at the college)

2. **Is the A-level course employer-funded or arranged as part of an employer-agreed future job?** (Most A-levels at sixth form college are not, but I need to confirm)

3. **Is Alex married?** (This wouldn't normally be an issue, but I need to check for completeness)

Can you confirm these details about Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's doing his A-levels full-time at the college - it's the normal school hours during the week. It's not anything to do with an employer, just regular sixth form. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex's situation is clear and sounds like it meets the approved education requirements. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not working at all?**

This is important because if a 16-19 year old works 24 hours or more per week AND is not in approved education/training, they wouldn't be eligible. However, since Alex is in full-time education, this is just a standard check we need to complete.

What's Alex's current work situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't work, which means he definitely works less than 24 hours per week. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, we're making progress! Now I need to check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, I need to know if Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

If he's not receiving either of these benefits, then he passes this check. Is Alex receiving any of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits himself. He's just a student living at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own right. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's apprenticeship status (though based on what you've told me, this should be straightforward):

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's studying A-levels at sixth form college, the answer should be no. But let me confirm - is he in any type of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Just doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me move to the next check, which is about your residency as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status as the claimant. There are several paths that can qualify you for Child Benefit. Let me ask:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward path
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme and are:**
   - Working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - Actively seeking work (can claim as jobseeker for up to 91 days), OR
   - Have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family financially, OR
   - Studying and have sufficient resources to support yourself, OR
   - A family member of an EEA or Swiss national with the right to reside
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries**

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirement - you normally live in the UK. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. There are a few ways this can be established:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** - This is the most straightforward path since you mentioned he lives at home with you in Manchester
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - This could include paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc. (at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount)
3. **You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement** - This wouldn't apply in your case

Since you've already told me Alex lives at home with you in Manchester, I believe the first path applies - you live with him. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're clearly responsible for Alex since he lives at home with you. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check an important detail:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is another relative or guardian claiming for him?

Or is it just you claiming for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're the only one claiming for Alex. Let me move to the next check about Alex's location.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's current living situation:

**Is Alex in any of the following situations:**

1. **In hospital** - Staying in hospital for medical treatment
2. **In care** - In local authority or voluntary sector care
3. **Fostered** - Living with foster carers
4. **Living normally** - At home with you or in normal accommodation

Based on what you've told me, Alex is living at home with you in Manchester. Is that correct, or is there any special circumstance I should know about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - he's just living at home with me normally. Nothing special about his living situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home with you normally. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! We're almost at the end of the assessment. Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for Alex's accommodation and upkeep yourself, or is the local council providing financial support towards his housing or maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm supporting him myself. He just lives at home with me and I pay for everything.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final piece of information I needed. You're supporting Alex yourself, and the council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me record your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **🎉 Good News! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

Congratulations! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex**.

### Why You're Eligible:

Alex meets all the eligibility requirements:
- ✅ He is 17 years old (within the qualifying age range)
- ✅ He is in **approved full-time education** (A-levels at sixth form college)
- ✅ He is not working full-time (not working at all)
- ✅ He is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own right
- ✅ He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You live together and are responsible for his upkeep
- ✅ No one else is claiming for him
- ✅ He's living normally at home
- ✅ The council is not paying towards his accommodation

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or use **form CH2** (apply by post)
2. **Gather required documents:**
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving license, etc.)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of address (utility bill, council tax bill, etc.)

3. **Important Note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earns over **£60,000 per year**, you may be liable for the High Income Child Benefit Charge
   - This is a tax charge that reduces or eliminates your Child Benefit, depending on income

4. **Payment frequency:**
   - Normally paid every 4 weeks
   - Weekly payments available if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits

### Reference:
For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Best of luck with your application!
